headline: Parliament Approves Critical Medicines Procurement Framework
deck: The deal ties public support to EU supply and lets five member states ask the Commission to procure on their behalf.
body: The European Parliament approved the Critical Medicines Act deal by 592 votes to 35, with 30 abstentions. The text still needs Council approval before it becomes European Union law. [E4] [E5]

Under the agreed framework, companies receiving national or European Union financial support must prioritise supply to the European Union market. Five member states, down from nine in the negotiations, will be enough to ask the European Commission to procure on their behalf. [E1] [E2] [E3]
